Definition: from G3624; domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent:--(those) of the (his own) house(-hold).
BiblicalUsage: Oikeios means of one's own house, a member of the household, a relative, one who belongs. Paul says to do good especially to those who are of the household of faith in Galatians 6:10, and that believers are fellow citizens with the saints and of the household of God in Ephesians 2:19. The hard edge is in 1 Timothy 5:8: a man who provides not for his own house has denied the faith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the household of God is the truest family there is, and its members owe each other the care of kin. That is why I hold that providing for your own is not a small duty, Paul says denying it is denying the faith.
